input.summary: P5 parlour (parts/room-41.mjs): 3x3 living room with a dark oak stair sofa facing the hall doorway, a chair, a spruce fence table with a top slab and potted poppy, a red carpet rug and one hanging lantern over the table. Drawn with layers() from a text grid.
left: Floor and ceiling are not built yet in the shared build: the y1 floor layer and the y5 ceiling under this box come from shell-east. Until then `mcd room` reports the carpet and lantern as floating (FIT) and the walk as unreachable (no doorway or floor). Re-run `$MCD room build.nbt --rooms rooms.json --only "P5 parlour"` after the shell merge.

Verified only in a scratch copy (/tmp/p48/mock.nbt) that adds a y1 floor, a y5 ceiling, walls and a doorway at x87 z15..17: walk 8 of 8 reachable, light min 10, FIT OK. The real cased opening on x87 must be left air by the shell, or the sofa/table lane is cut off.

plan.md's Checklist covers parts 1-6 only, and the elements.md 'Per house' rooms item covers all eight houses, so I did not tick anything. The parlour meets the 'no dark cell' rule (light 8+ on every floor cell in the mock).

waste.what: Worked out the 3x3 furniture layout cell by cell and wrote the stair facings (sofa and chair backs) by hand, then checked each placement by re-running make.sh.
waste.cost: About 3 make.sh runs and 1 scratch mock for the floor, ceiling and walls.
waste.tool: A `mcd room --assume-shell <room>` mode that lays a temporary floor, ceiling and doorway around the box, so the walk and lantern checks work before the other shell parts are merged.

waste.what: Verifying walk and light before the shell existed meant writing my own mock script (/tmp/p48/mock.mjs) by hand: fill floor, ceiling, walls and the doorway.
waste.tool: `mcd room build.nbt --rooms rooms.json --only <room> --mock-shell` or a `--rooms` box option that assumes walls around the box.

waste.what: Reading the stair facing convention (back side vs. front) from the toolkit text, since the furnisher's chair and sofa rules depend on it.
waste.tool: A `mcd states dark_oak_stairs` example line in the vocabulary with a worked chair example (`B.stairs(mat, facing-of-back)`).

companions.task: Lay the y1 floor layer and the y5 ceiling over the parlour box (x84..86 z15..17) and leave the cased opening on x87 z15..17 open, so the lantern hangs from a solid block and the walk reaches the sofa.
Pick the sofa and chair cloth (red and dark oak carpet, a second stair seat) so the parlour reads as a sitting room from the doorway.
